definition: A trained behavior where the model declines harmful or out-of-policy requests.
details: A trained behavior where the model declines harmful or out-of-policy requests. Calibrating refusals (refusing what should be refused, and nothing more) is a core post-training quality axis; over-refusal is itself a failure mode.

explainer.lead: A trained behavior where the model declines harmful or out-of-policy requests. It matters because calibrating refusals is a core post-training quality axis.

tiers.eli5: It's the model saying 'I can't help with that' when asked to do something it shouldn't — and knowing when not to say it.
tiers.practitioner: Post-training tunes what the model refuses; the pitfall is over-refusal, which is itself a failure mode — the model should refuse what should be refused, and nothing more.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a trained behavior where the model declines harmful or out-of-policy requests; calibration requires refusing what should be refused and nothing more, with over-refusal counted as a failure mode.

explainer.example: The model declines a request for harmful content but still answers a benign question that merely mentions the same topic.
